newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Monsoon winds cause Hong Kong cargo backlog.
newsitem.headline: Monsoon winds cause Hong Kong cargo backlog.

text.p: Monsoon wind conditions have caused a backlog of air cargo in Hong Kong, say airlines.
Air France Cargo said all carriers are being affected on both European and trans-Pacific long haul routes by having to suddenly off-load pallets.
The size of the backlog from all airlines is more than 400 tonnes, said the airline's regional cargo manager for Hong Kong, China, Macau, Taiwan and South Korea, Philippe Bour.
"Everybody is being hit by these weather conditions and customers are unhappy about having their cargo left behind - but so are we," Bour added.

"On one flight last week we had a Boeing 747 Combi leave with only 10 tonnes aboard. And on another freighter flight everything was perfect until half an hour before departure when we had to offload 10 tonnes all because of the tail wind conditions. It is the first time I have ever known so much cargo having to be offladed," he said.
The backlog is thought to be one reason why airlines have agreed to increase cargo rates to Europe for the second time this month as demand continues to exceed supply.
Air France says it expects some of the backlog to be cleared this weekend because of a lull in activity partly because factories in China have been enjoying a three day holiday.

Other major carriers contacted by Reuters confirmed the backlog. A spokesman for British Airways Plc World Cargo which has two daily flights to London from Hong Kong said it was "really suffering." --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
